unresolved_added: The six-species table says only that some parameters come from the appendix of [5]; it does not identify a source per cell, publish the source rows, state extension-rate units, distinguish measured from author-selected values, or carry uncertainty. Every downstream fit and regional simulation therefore inherits untraceable point parameters.

The notation ledger gives T a malformed temperature unit in the extracted/printed artifact, gives V_E only a numeric scope rather than a physical unit, defines G and F_i as integer sets without a biomass or mass mapping, and mixes probability, cell count, rate, and time interfaces without a dimensional ledger.

T is multiplied directly by the square root of V_E and added to an offset without a fitted coefficient or unit conversion. The claimed half-order magnitude does not close the dimensions of a 122-day decomposition fraction, and the temperature multiplier is not derived from the cited trait relation.

The log base, zero-rate handling, coefficient evidence, residuals, and observed M-versus-log(V_D) points are absent. Exponentiating and reparameterizing the asserted relation is algebraically clear, but the current paper supplies no data display or uncertainty supporting the relation it later fits.

The extension component, exponential moisture component, and intercept are added without a dimensional argument, interaction term, model-form comparison, or range constraint. The paper does not show that this additive form is preferable to alternatives or remains inside V_D in [0,1].

The response is called an Arrhenius diagram, but its exponent uses V_Emax divided by T times H rather than activation energy divided by a gas constant and absolute temperature. Extension rate, temperature, and humidity do not form an evidently dimensionless exponent, so the physical Arrhenius interpretation is unsupported.

At T=T_max the equation returns V_Emax times exp[-V_Emax/(T_max H)], not V_Emax, even though T_max is described as the optimum and V_Emax as the theoretical maximum. Figure 1 accordingly peaks well below each labeled maximum; the naming and mathematical value are not reconciled.

The exponential branches are undefined at T=0 or H=0 even though their printed domains include T=0 and H is declared on [0,1]. The separate outside-domain zero branch does not resolve these in-branch singularities, and no limiting convention is stated.

The official moisture trade-off is described as competitive ranking minus moisture niche width, yet Equation 6 replaces it with a linear transform of an ambient-humidity lower limit. No paired data, scale reconciliation, or biological calibration establishes that these two constructs are equivalent.

Equation 7 declares lambda, a, and K to be arbitrary real numbers, but a^M is not generally real for a negative a and noninteger M; Table 2 uses fractional negative M. The optimization needs at least a positivity constraint on a and a stated admissible domain.

The fitting dataset is referenced only as an appendix of [5]. The paper omits N, the actual {T,V_E,M,V_D} rows, exclusions, duplicate handling, units, and any train/validation split, so the objective and reported coefficients cannot be independently reconstructed.

Unweighted training squared error is the only fit criterion. There are no parameter bounds, regularization, identifiability analysis, multiple starts, holdout error, coefficient uncertainty, residual diagnostics, or comparison with simpler and alternative nonlinear forms.

The learning rate r, iteration budget I, sample count N, sampling order, seed, numerical precision, and stopping rule are not reported. A reader cannot reproduce the SGD path or determine whether the final iterate is stable to hyperparameters or initialization.

The pseudocode sets t=mod(k,N); with the conventional remainder this produces t=0 whenever k is divisible by N, while the displayed dataset is indexed from 1 to N. The zero-versus-one-based sample convention is not resolved.

The a update does not enforce a>0 even though later evaluations use a^M with fractional negative M. Crossing zero can make the objective or gradient non-real, and the paper supplies no reparameterization, projection, feasibility check, or gradient verification.

Only loss and lambda are plotted for one run; a and K are not shown. The loss remains highly noisy and no final loss, RMSE, R2, validation error, parameter tolerance, repeat agreement, or global-optimum evidence supports the statement that the nonlinear fit converges effectively.

One coefficient triple is transferred to every species and environment without species effects or uncertainty. The fitted response is not constrained to the declared V_D range [0,1], and the paper does not report how negative or above-one predictions are handled before conversion to decomposition time.

For positive V_E, sigmoid(1/V_E) decreases from near 1 toward 0.5 as V_E increases. This directly contradicts the prose claim that P_E increases with extension rate and means the proposed probability transform reverses the intended rate ordering.

Equation 5 explicitly returns V_E=0 outside the temperature domain, but Equation 15 then evaluates 1/V_E and is undefined. No zero-rate branch, limiting value, cap, or inactive-species rule is stated.

The set update adds a generic (p,q) after prose discusses an uninfected cell adjacent to F_i, but the equation does not encode neighborhood, eligibility, simultaneous claims, species collision priority, or update ordering. Removal timing relative to addition and grid-label updates is also incomplete.

If N_i^{t+1}=|F_i^{t+1}| is computed after Equation 17 removes fully decomposed cells, subtracting N_Di^t again double-counts removals. The expression is also called dN_i/dt although it is a discrete difference with no division by or definition of the time step.

The correction factor c=5x10^6 is asserted without derivation or calibration. Dividing a global 122-day mass-loss fraction by 500^2 makes cell time depend on arbitrary grid resolution, while cell mass, rounding, zero/negative V_D handling, and resolution invariance are absent.

The prose resets fully decomposed cells to G(p,q)=1 to simulate falling leaves, but Equation 20 only removes coordinates from F_i and contains no renewal arrival process, timing, or resource amount. This hidden nutrient input affects both late stabilization and decomposition totals.

The pseudocode performs infection work when G(p_j,q_j) is not equal to 1, even though the prose defines G=1 as uninfected and says fungi infect uninfected adjacent cells. The printed condition therefore appears reversed relative to the stated cellular semantics.

Repeated line numbers obscure nesting, and the algorithm omits random draws, collision resolution, grid boundaries, decomposition-age counters, completed-cell selection, falling-leaf renewal, regional T/H inputs, decomposition-rate accumulation, seeds, and replicate loops. It cannot reproduce Figures 3-9 end to end.

Population panels end at day 100 or 60 while the paper reports decomposition after 122 days. Exact initialization, random seed, cell-to-population scale, late-level calculation, replicate variation, and the rule producing the reported 0.68 decomposition rate are not published.

The paper discusses mutual benefit and exclusion but then treats fungal-fungal interaction as competition only, citing broad interaction literature rather than data for the selected species. This is a scenario reduction, not evidence that facilitation, metabolite exchange, or pair-specific effects can be ignored.

For a remaining factor between 0 and 1, dividing V_E by that factor makes 1/[V_E(1-occupancy)] larger, so the sigmoid P_C is larger than P_E, not lower as the prose claims. Together with Equation 15, the algebra reverses the intended competitive suppression.

N_j is already defined as a number yet appears as |N_j|; the competitor index set, exclusion of species i, simultaneous versus lagged counts, and spatial locality are unspecified. At full or overfull summed occupancy the remaining factor is zero or negative, and no domain rule is provided.

The competitive CA inherits the zero-rate singularity, occupancy-denominator failure, reversed probability direction, hidden renewal, collision ambiguity, and uncalibrated decomposition time. Replacing one probability does not by itself establish a biologically valid interaction model.

The 33.65% population reduction and 42.69% decomposition reduction are reported without a formula, exact comparison time, matched random seeds, repeated runs, confidence interval, or sensitivity to initialization. A single stochastic realization cannot support precise average-percentage language.

Short and long run are not formally defined, and the explanation relies on 100-day constructed trajectories with a hidden falling-leaf renewal process. No interaction metric, resource balance, crossover time, or independent observation validates the claimed horizon change.

The dependency graph labels the parameter data as [18], while Sections 3.1.5 and Equation 8 state that the fitting data come from [5]. Reference [18] concerns tropical litter quality rather than the trait-data appendix, so the central provenance arrow is internally inconsistent.

The four panels do not form a clean one-factor design: one panel changes both T and H, the displayed humidity shifts are not the 8% change implied by the Summary, and exact dominance times are not defined. No sensitivity coefficient, joint interaction, uncertainty band, or decision-reversal threshold is computed.

Static T-H point perturbations are used to discuss future atmospheric and seasonal change. The model includes no time-varying weather series, trend, frequency, autocorrelation, precipitation, drought duration, or climate projection, so it does not directly answer the atmospheric-trend requirement.

Each environment is represented by one temperature-humidity point with coordinates but no location name, date range, season, averaging window, measurement quality, distribution, or uncertainty. One observation cannot represent an arid, semi-arid, temperate, arboreal, or tropical-rainforest climate.

Arboreal is a vegetation/habitat descriptor rather than a climate class, yet it receives one T-H coordinate like the climate zones. The paper does not define the required arboreal environment, its tree/substrate conditions, or why the selected coordinate represents it.

The arboreal prose names Trichoderma, Hyphomycetes, and Gibberella, but Hyphomycetes is absent from Table 2 and the Figure 8 legend instead shows Trichoderma, Fusarium, and Gibberella. The simulated combination and resulting dominance claim are internally inconsistent.

Dominant, inferior, suitable, and persistent have no formal metric, evaluation horizon, threshold, tie rule, or uncertainty rule. Several curves are still rising or crossing near day 100, and different species sets across regions prevent controlled cross-region comparison.

The 68.29% decomposition rate after 122 days is not visible in Figure 8, Table 5, the pseudocode, or an equation trace from cell states. The paper explicitly omits the other regional rates for page limits, preventing reconstruction or comparison of this headline value.

The left legend names 'Only Aflatoxin', which is a toxin and not one of the selected fungal species; the intended species is ambiguous. The right panel does not say which single-species denominator is used per test, so the 1000 ratios and mean 2.89 are not reproducible.

The paper does not show that single- and three-species runs have matched initial total cells, biomass, occupied area, resource supply, random seeds, or decomposition accounting. More initial agents or opportunities could create a multi-species advantage unrelated to biodiversity.

Biodiversity is operationalized only as three selected species versus one. There is no richness gradient, evenness, functional diversity, larger community, perturbation, recovery, resilience, stability metric, field validation, or uncertainty; a noisy ratio series that sometimes approaches zero does not establish guaranteed robustness.

Terms such as accurate, precise, robust, good generalization, and high consistency are stronger than the evidence: there is no held-out prediction test or field comparison. The Article also presents broad role percentages and ecosystem claims without inline citations or clear separation between established biology and this paper's simulations.

There is no Appendix or code listing despite a nonlinear SGD fit, 500-by-500 stochastic CA, multi-species collisions, resource renewal, regional scenarios, and 1000 repeats. Data rows, hyperparameters, initialization, seeds, decomposition calculation, plots, and outputs are all missing, so none of the headline rates or ratios can be reproduced end to end.
